raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image-2.1 with `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` never replays a captured graph for a prompt whose length differs from the warmup placeholder. On GB300 (main 3831e7e09) the warmup captures 33 segments with 72 inputs, yet every real request logs `serving signature MISSED` and runs eager, on 1 GPU and under TP2 alike.

`QwenImage21DenoisingStage` disables prompt padding on purpose. Prefill (step 0) is eager anyway. After it, a DiT step reads nothing of the prompt except each layer's prefix K/V and the target RoPE, and the K/V are at the exact prompt length. 72 = 4 step inputs + 4 layout tensors + 32 layers x K/V.

## Modifications

- `model_padders/qwen_image21.py` acts only on cached steps (single sample, caches filled, sp == 1). It left-pads the prefix K/V to the text bucket and stacks all layers into one tensor, so a replay copies one input instead of 64. It also drops the prefill-only inputs and adds a 0-d `prefix_pad`. A prefix longer than the largest bucket is left alone; the runner reports the miss once.
- The DiT's target attention runs at a model-level `eager_on_graph` break point (`attend_past_prefix_pad`). It reads the live pad once per forward and slices `k[:, pad:]`. Because the pad is on the left, the valid K/V form one strided view, so the kernel receives exactly the eager K/V.
- The stage-level override that disabled padding is removed.

## Accuracy Tests

BCG against eager, four prompt lengths (including ~350 tokens in the 512 bucket): bit-identical (max_abs = 0), on 1x H200, on 2x H200 TP2 and on 2x GB300 TP2. Before this PR the comparison was trivially identical, because every request ran eager.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image-2.1 1024x1024, served. Median of 5 per round, three interleaved rounds; the arms differ only in `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph`.

| | eager | BCG, this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1x H200 | 4.521 / 4.525 / 4.518 s | 4.546 / 4.540 / 4.544 s (+0.5%) |
| 2x H200, TP2 | 2.788 / 2.790 / 2.792 s | **2.737 / 2.731 / 2.740 s (−1.9%)** |

On one H200 the step is GPU-bound (103 ms), so replay saves no launch time. What remains is BCG's own cost: each attention break copies its output into the bridge buffer, plus 33 graph launches. Under TP2 each rank's GPU work halves, the launch cost shows, and BCG wins.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests:
  - `test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py`: prefix lengths in one bucket share a signature, and calls without a replayable prefix are not padded.
  - `test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`: one captured graph replays bit-exact across prompt lengths.

  On GB300 (main 5730345 + this PR), with `test_qwen_image21.py`: 141 passed.
- [ ] Update documentation: N/A.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

This PR and its sibling PR for Qwen-Image / 2512 padding both edit `prompt_padding.py` and `test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py`. Whichever lands second may need a trivial rebase.

+# Copyright 2023-2026 SGLang Team
+# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0
+# ==============================================================================
+"""Qwen-Image 2.1 breakable CUDA graph (BCG) prompt padding.
+
+Only cached steps replay graphs: prefill runs eagerly and stores each layer's
+prefix K/V at its exact length, and a cached step reads nothing else of the
+prompt. The padder left-pads that K/V to the text bucket, stacks it into one
+tensor (one input copy per replay) and drops the prefill-only inputs, so prompts
+of different lengths share one signature. The pad rows never reach attention or
+RoPE: the DiT attends past them at a graph break, so replays stay bit-exact with
+the unpadded eager forward.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.breakable_cuda_graph import (
+    prompt_padding as bcg_utils,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.distributed import get_sp_world_size
+
+
+def is_qwen_image21_transformer(current_model: Any, call_kwargs: dict) -> bool:
+    return (
+        bcg_utils.transformer_class_name_matches(current_model, "qwenimage21")
+        and "prefix_caches" in call_kwargs
+    )
+
+
+def pad_qwen_image21_prompt_kwargs(
+    call_kwargs: dict, current_model: Any, buckets: tuple[int, ...]
+) -> dict:
+    caches = call_kwargs["prefix_caches"]
+    # only cached single-sample steps replay: prefill runs eagerly, warmup
+    # captures one sample, and the SP attention path has no pad-aware break
+    if (
+        caches is None
+        or len(caches) != 1
+        or not caches[0][0]
+        or get_sp_world_size() != 1
+    ):
+        return call_kwargs
+    seq = caches[0][0]["key"].shape[1]
+    # a longer prefix (e.g. an edit's condition-image tokens) runs eagerly; the
+    # runner reports that miss once, so skip the per-step bucket warning
+    bucket = next((bucket for bucket in buckets if seq <= bucket), None)
+    if bucket is None:
+        return call_kwargs
+    rows = torch.stack(
+        [tensor for cache in caches[0] for tensor in (cache["key"], cache["value"])]
+    )
+    prefix_kv = rows.new_zeros(*rows.shape[:2], bucket, *rows.shape[3:])
+    prefix_kv[:, :, bucket - seq :] = rows
+    return dict(
+        call_kwargs,
+        encoder_hidden_states=None,
+        encoder_hidden_states_mask=None,
+        condition_latents=None,
+        layouts=[{"target_rope": call_kwargs["layouts"][0]["target_rope"]}],
+        prefix_caches=None,
+        prefix_kv=prefix_kv,
+        prefix_pad=torch.tensor(bucket - seq),
+    )
+
+
+bcg_utils.register_prompt_padder(
+    is_qwen_image21_transformer, pad_qwen_image21_prompt_kwargs
+)
